description:
## Why
A variable is identified only by its spelling. Observed on the current binary, with Elixir's answer in brackets:
- a macro's `t = 99` overwrites the caller's `t` (Elixir: 1);
- a macro reads the caller's `t` (Elixir: undefined variable "t" (context M));
- a second expansion reads the first expansion's `t` (Elixir: the same error);
- `__fz_capture_arg_1 = 999; f = &(&1 + __fz_capture_arg_1); f.(1)` returns 2 (Elixir: 1000).

## Approved design (../fz-p8p.22.html, revision 2)
- `src/ast`: `Var { name, context }`, with `VarContext = User | Macro(FunctionId, u32) | Generated(u32)`. `Expr::Var`, `Pattern::Var`, `Pattern::Pinned`, the name in `Pattern::As` and `BitSize::Var` carry a `Var`. Every map that resolves a variable is keyed by `Var`: the lowering env, the lambda free/bound sets (body.rs:4519-4779), and dispatch_matrix `binding_subjects` / `pinned_by_name`.
- One var-node constructor (`QuotedSourceBuilder::variable`), using Elixir's layout: the context goes in the third slot (nil for user code, the macro's FunctionId inside its quote), and the expansion counter goes in meta. The front door, quote lowering (body.rs:1333) and sugar (source_sugar.rs:443) all use it. Decode (quoted_function.rs:306) builds the `Var`.
- One stamping walk per expansion, run after `run_macro_on_source` (quoted_expander.rs:472) and before memoization. The ordinal is local to the job attempt and advances once per macro call visited, cache hit or not. There is no global counter and no pointer-derived id.
- Sugar parameters get `Generated(k)`. `capture_arg_name`, `lambda_arg_name` and sugar's own `variable()` are deleted.
- `var!/1` is an ordinary macro in lib/runtime.fz. `var!/2` is fz-p8p.25.
- An undefined macro variable reports `lower/unbound`, and the message names the macro.
- Deleted: the lexical-context write on var nodes (source.rs:399-401 and the slot write), `META_LEXICAL_KEY`, and `QuotedLexicalContextKind::Source` / `Generated`. `Definition` / `Caller` stay, because they build __ENV__/__CALLER__.
- Docs: macro-expansion.md (one context concept; `bound_callable` is its eager call-side half) and the macros guide.

## Done when
- 00117 asserts `t == 1` and moves to fixtures/. port_macros_test.rs is deleted.
- New fixtures, all red before the change: `read_t` and `step` (`lower/unbound`); `var!` reaching the caller (asserts {10, 1}); the capture spelling collision (asserts 1000); a hygienic `case` pattern and a hygienic `size(n)` inside a quote.
- 00118 and 00119 are green, and no other golden moves.
- The canon of the `step` and `var!` programs is identical across two drives.
## Build path
A first build is parked on branch fz-p8p.22/wip-v1 (816e51f06), at findings ccffbd28f. It found two blockers: fz-p8p.26 (a macro's false arrives boxed and reads as truthy) and fz-p8p.27 (quote bodies round-trip through Expr and lose patterns, case, fn and bitstrings). Replay wip-v1 on top of both. Quote lowering's var-node construction then sits in .27's single walk. 00587 and 00588 are rewritten with quote instead of hand-built tuples, and 00584/00585 go green. The wip-v1 builder claimed that a macro call in any pattern fails; that is false (ident(t) = 5 in main works), so don't carry it forward.
title: Macro hygiene: quoted variables carry a context
